\chapter{What Was Going On}
\label{ch:ur-what-was-going-on}
\hlchaptermodality{266}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say what was going on in the past (voh paṛh rahī thī), set a scene with jab … to, and say during with daurān.}

Complete UR-R266-what-was-going-on: say what was going on, and what happened in the middle of it.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{پڑھ} \ur{رہا} \ur{تھا} (paṛh rahā thā)}{پڑھ رہا تھا (paṛh rahā thā)}]{\ur{پڑھ} \ur{رہا} \ur{تھا} (paṛh rahā thā) — what was going on}

\label{lesson:UR-C266-parh-raha-tha}



\begin{quote}
Say \textquotedblleft{}I used to read\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{maiṅ paṛhtā thā}.) That is a habit. This lesson is one moment in the past, with something still going on.
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: was doing}]
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{سو} \ur{رہی} \ur{تھی۔}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{so rahī thī.} — \textquotedblleft{}She was sleeping.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

Ask what Sara was doing last night, and the answer is three words: the stem \textbf{\ur{سو}} (\emph{so}), then \textbf{\ur{رہی}} (\emph{rahī}), then \textbf{\ur{تھی}} (\emph{thī}). Both follow Sara:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{سارا} \ur{سو} \ur{رہی} \ur{تھی۔}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Sārā so rahī thī.} — \textquotedblleft{}Sara was sleeping.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{میں} \ur{خط} \ur{لکھ} \ur{رہا} \ur{تھا۔}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{maiṅ khat likh rahā thā.} — \textquotedblleft{}I was writing a letter.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

A verb with an object takes no \textbf{\ur{نے}} (\emph{ne}) here: the writing was still going on.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{ہم} \ur{کھانا} \ur{کھا} \ur{رہے} \ur{تھے۔}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ham khānā khā rahe the.} — \textquotedblleft{}We were eating.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{who} & \textbf{was doing} \\
\midrule
a man & \textbf{\ur{رہا} \ur{تھا}} (\emph{rahā thā}) \\
a woman & \textbf{\ur{رہی} \ur{تھی}} (\emph{rahī thī}) \\
men; \textbf{\ur{ہم}}; \textbf{\ur{آپ}} & \textbf{\ur{رہے} \ur{تھے}} (\emph{rahe the}) \\
women & \textbf{\ur{رہی} \ur{تھیں}} (\emph{rahī thīṅ}) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: the scene and the event}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{باہر} \ur{بارش} \ur{ہو} \ur{رہی} \ur{تھی۔}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bāhar bārish ho rahī thī.} — \textquotedblleft{}It was raining outside.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

That is a scene: going on, with no edge. Drop an event into it with \textbf{\ur{جب}} (\emph{jab}), \textquotedblleft{}when\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\ur{تو}} (\emph{to}), \textquotedblleft{}then\textquotedblright{}:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{جب} \ur{میں} \ur{گھر} \ur{آیا،}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jab maiṅ ghar āyā,}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{تو} \ur{سارا} \ur{سو} \ur{رہی} \ur{تھی۔}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{to Sārā so rahī thī.} — \textquotedblleft{}When I came home, Sara was sleeping.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

This \textbf{\ur{تو}} is \emph{to}, \textquotedblleft{}then\textquotedblright{}, not \textbf{\ur{تو}} \emph{tū}, \textquotedblleft{}you\textquotedblright{}: the romanization tells them apart. \textbf{\ur{آیا}} (\emph{āyā}) is the event, over in a moment. \textbf{\ur{سو} \ur{رہی} \ur{تھی}} is the scene it cut into.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textquotedblleft{}I was reading\textquotedblright{} — \emph{maiṅ paṛh rahā thā}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}She was reading\textquotedblright{} — \emph{voh paṛh rahī thī}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}We were reading\textquotedblright{} — \emph{ham paṛh rahe the}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\textquotedblleft{}She was writing a letter\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\ur{وہ} \ur{خط} \ur{لکھ} \ur{رہی} \ur{تھی}}.) Does it take \textbf{\ur{نے}}? (No: it was still going on.) In the sentence about coming home, which verb is the event? (\textbf{\ur{آیا}}.) And which is the scene? (\textbf{\ur{سو} \ur{رہی} \ur{تھی}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{دوران} (daurān)}{دوران (daurān)}]{\ur{دوران} (daurān) — during}

\label{lesson:UR-C266-dauran}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say \textquotedblleft{}it was raining\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{bārish ho rahī thī}.) Then \textquotedblleft{}a journey\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{safar}.)
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{دوران}}
\textbf{\ur{دوران}} — \emph{daurān} — \textquotedblleft{}during\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{سفر} \ur{کے} \ur{دوران} \ur{بارش} \ur{ہوئی۔}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{safar ke daurān bārish huī.} — \textquotedblleft{}It rained during the journey.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

It stands after its noun, with \textbf{\ur{کے}} (\emph{ke}) in front of it, as in \textbf{\ur{کے} \ur{لیے}} (\emph{ke liye}).

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{کھانے} \ur{کے} \ur{دوران} \ur{وہ} \ur{آیا۔}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{khāne ke daurān voh āyā.} — \textquotedblleft{}He came during the meal.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\textbf{\ur{کھانا}} (\emph{khānā}) becomes \textbf{\ur{کھانے}} (\emph{khāne}) before \textbf{\ur{کے}}, as most masculine nouns in -\ur{ا} do.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{دوران}} (\emph{daurān}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{dawarān}, \textquotedblleft{}a turning round\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{daurān}, then \emph{safar ke daurān}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}During the meal she came\textquotedblright{} — \emph{khāne ke daurān voh āī}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}During the journey I was reading\textquotedblright{} — \emph{safar ke daurān maiṅ paṛh rahā thā}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \textbf{\ur{دوران}} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}During\textquotedblright{}.) \textquotedblleft{}During the journey\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\ur{سفر} \ur{کے} \ur{دوران}}.) What comes in front of it? (\textbf{\ur{کے}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(review)]{Review — what was going on}

\label{lesson:UR-R266-what-was-going-on}



\begin{quote}
Say \textquotedblleft{}Sara wrote a letter\textquotedblright{} and \textquotedblleft{}I will go\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{Sārā ne khat likhā}, \emph{maiṅ jāūṅ gā}.)
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item I was writing a letter. Sara was reading.
  \item It was raining outside.
  \item When I came home, Sara was sleeping.
  \item During the journey it was raining.
  \item He came during the meal.
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\textquotedblleft{}We were eating\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\ur{ہم} \ur{کھا} \ur{رہے} \ur{تھے}}.) Now the other way round: what does \textbf{\ur{رہی} \ur{تھیں}} tell you? (Women, and something going on.) In \textbf{\ur{جب} … \ur{تو} …}, which half is the event? (The \textbf{\ur{جب}} half, in the plain past.) \textquotedblleft{}During the journey\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\ur{سفر} \ur{کے} \ur{دوران}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
